requirements.requirement: Repair /srv/legacy2/file-descriptor-leak/bin/read-documents.py so it completes at least 500 successive reads with a soft open-file limit of 64 and reports the same document length on every read.
requirements.summary: The repaired command completed 500 reads at soft limit 64 with exit 0, exactly 500 output lines, unique length 42, no incorrect lines, and empty stderr. The same behavior was demonstrated again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure opened resources are closed when document processing fails.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses a context-managed open. Injected read-failure tests before and after restart showed one open and one close while propagating the failure.

requirements.summary: The document retained its baseline SHA-256 of 88fe7058122f278cca094fad2c26108a2b401dd1ecddc14d330ff0eed96377ff. The persisted script still derives the loop count from sys.argv[1].

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged after execution and restart. The repaired Python command ran successfully using the installed interpreter.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart evidence. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart behavior and boot identity were recorded, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af to d93a3558-9a63-4f95-9450-0867669b1062, and the repaired script, document identity, platform, services, sockets, and package health recovered coherently.
limitations: The injected failure test exercises an exception during read after a successful open, rather than open() itself raising. The context-managed implementation directly demonstrates cleanup of an acquired resource; if open() raises, no file resource has been acquired to close.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The target replacement was the required repair; temporary output files were bounded and cleaned. Syntax validation generated a bytecode artifact during cmd-47cc308401c84562, but it served validation and was fully removed by cmd-8642c57679d546ed. The transient reboot scheduling in cmd-74a23dcd53e24f4f was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, unchanged package health and exposure, and only expected reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes.
